text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- America should help Vietnam deal with the consequences of the wartime use of the agent orange defoliant, Communist Party General Secretary Do Muoi told visiting U.S Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin earlier this week.
-- The National Assembly is expected to pass Vietnam's first Trade Law soon, which is aimed at ensuring a multi-sector economy activated by the market mechanism with a socialist orientation.
-- National Assembly deputies have voiced doubts about a proposed north-south expressway project.
-- An Interior Ministry mission, headed by minister Le Minh Huong, began an official visit to Beijing last week.
-- North Korean Deputy Prime Minister Kong Jin-tae has held meetings with Vietnamese officials to promote economic ties.
-- The Prime Minister has issued a directive aimed at combatting crime and social disorder.
-- Vietnam Airlines carried 711,600 passengers and 10,600 tonnes of cargo during the first quarter of 1997.
-- Seven children were killed and 34 injured when a fragmentation bomb exploded in the central province of Nghe An earlier this week.
-- Vietnam is preparing for negotiations with the United States on a copyright accord.
